text:
Function-based evaluation fits this audit better than treating co-purchases as proof of complementarity. [TREC’s protocol](https://trec-product-search.github.io/recommendations.html) defines substitutes as serving the same function and complements as adding, powering, or enhancing functionality. [Function-Based Labels (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.03945) develops explicit relationship definitions and a human-annotated dataset of 2,759 product pairs, addressing ambiguity in behavior-derived labels. These relationships describe products; they do not establish a particular user’s purchase intent, replacement need, or equipment ownership.

Explanation evaluation should check individual claims against available evidence. [On the Factual Consistency of Text-based Explainable Recommendation Models (2025–2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24366) finds that strong semantic similarity can coexist with poor statement-level factual precision. Its review-derived evidence is unavailable here, but its atomic-claim evaluation approach transfers to titles, descriptions, and histories. Compatibility research explicitly distinguishes [compatible, incompatible, and unknown](https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.04499); that older work uses product Q&A, so its evidence source cannot be imported into this task.

Proposed adaptation: annotate each recommendation against a named history item, recording timestamps and exact supporting metadata spans. Keep separate fields for relationship (complement/substitute/other/unknown), compatibility (supported/conflict/unknown/not applicable), and purchase intent (usually unknown). Require explicit contradictory specifications for a conflict; missing equipment information means unknown. Recent purchases support only a possible-substitute flag. Pilot the rubric with two independent annotators, report raw agreement and Cohen’s κ per field before adjudication, and retain unknown rates and disagreement examples. Report audit findings separately from macro validation HR@10; metadata support does not establish faithfulness to the model’s actual reasoning.
